pages.title: End of Dimension Tips
pages.text: This chapter covers some tips and or tricks for rounding out this simulation.

pages.title: Efficient pigiron
pages.text: In the more modern incarnation of the Alloy kiln, the $(item)Induction Smelter$() can smelt $(item)Pigiron Ingots$() more efficiently. Only requiring 1 $(item)Iron ingot$() per $(item)Bloody mud$().

pages.title: Automated starmetal
pages.text: You could quite easily automate $(item)Starmetal$() using $(item)Mechanical Users$(), $(item)Mechanical Miners$() and $(item)Scanners$().$(br2)Set this up where you found your first floating crystal.

If you're willing to go the extra mile in this simulation you can get a $(item)Quarry card$().$(br2)This will allow you to $(item)GREATLY$() improve your $(item)Resource Gathering Capabilities$() using the $(item)Builder$().

pages.title: Quarry Card Setup
pages.text: The easiest way to quarry with the $(item)Quarry Card$() is Sneak right clicking with it in the air, then manually define a quite big box, like 100x90x100.$(br2)Then in the builder you can press one of the top-right buttons to align the box to one of the builder corners.$(br2)This is far more efficient then manually marking corners with the $(item)Quarry Card$().
The $(item)Filter$() is a great complement to the quarry card.$(br2)It can blacklist or whitelist items from the builder, either preventing or allowing the quarrying of items.

pages.title: Quarry Filter Setup
pages.text: A good way of setting up the filter is taking a mining trip, while holding the filter, you can add ores to the whitelist by $(item)SHIFT right clicking$() them.$(br2)Once you've found each ore, the filter is complete, and you can put it in a builder. The builder will now only care about mining ores.$(br2)Neat right?!

pages.title: Quarry Power
pages.text: Quarrying even with a filter takes a lot of $(item)Power$().$(br2)2 solid power generation methods are covered in the start of the next chapter.
